{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows low positivity (0.00) and true prices show persistent downward drift.",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent high prices (last 3-5 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.33), to avoid underestimating upward momentum.",
    "Apply a downward bias correction when model overestimates prices after a recent spike (e.g., >70.00), especially if sentiment is flat or negative.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility when true prices show mean reversion toward lower levels (e.g., from 75+ to 65–70), especially after 3+ consecutive days of high prices.",
    "If sentiment history includes a recent 0.33 (positive signal), increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential bullish momentum, but cap at 75.00 to avoid overshoot.",
    "When true prices are consistently below 65.00 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect bearish trend, regardless of sentiment.",
    "Avoid forecasting spikes above 75.00 unless sentiment history includes 0.33 for 2+ consecutive days — otherwise, cap forecasts at 74.00 to prevent overreaction."
  ]
}
